78	def _validate_fields(fields: list[FieldSpec]) -> list[tuple[str, str, int, int]]:
79	    if not fields:
80	        raise RequestInvalidError("Field list must not be empty")
81	
82	    cleaned: list[tuple[str, str, bool]] = []
83	    seen: set[str] = set()
84	    for field in fields:
85	        field_name = field.name.strip()
86	        field_type = field.type.strip()
87	        if not field_name:
88	            raise RequestInvalidError("Field name must not be empty")
89	        if not field_type:
90	            raise RequestInvalidError(
91	                f"Field '{field_name}' is missing a non-empty type"
92	            )
93	        key = field_name
94	        if key in seen:
95	            raise RequestInvalidError(f"Duplicate field name '{field_name}' in version")
96	        seen.add(key)
97	        cleaned.append((field_name, field_type, field.nullable))
98	
99	    return [
100	        (name, ftype, 1 if nullable else 0, position)
101	        for position, (name, ftype, nullable) in enumerate(cleaned)
102	    ]

105	def create_schema_version(
106	    conn: sqlite3.Connection, dataset_name: str, fields: list[FieldSpec]
107	) -> dict:
108	    dataset = require_dataset(conn, dataset_name)
109	    validated = _validate_fields(fields)
110	
111	    next_version = conn.execute(
112	        "SELECT COALESCE(MAX(version), 0) + 1 AS next_version "
113	        "FROM schema_versions WHERE dataset_id = ?",
114	        (dataset["id"],),
115	    ).fetchone()["next_version"]
116	    created_at = utc_now_iso()
117	
118	    try:
119	        version_cursor = conn.execute(
120	            "INSERT INTO schema_versions (dataset_id, version, created_at) "
121	            "VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
122	            (dataset["id"], next_version, created_at),
123	        )
124	    except sqlite3.IntegrityError as exc:
125	        raise ConflictError(
126	            f"Schema version {next_version} of dataset '{dataset_name}' was "
127	            "created concurrently; retry to receive the next version number"
128	        ) from exc
129	    version_id = version_cursor.lastrowid
130	    conn.executemany(
131	        "INSERT INTO schema_fields (version_id, name, type, nullable, position) "
132	        "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
133	        [(version_id, name, ftype, nullable, position) for name, ftype, nullable, position in validated],
134	    )
135	    # A new version of this dataset may become part of future impact answers;
136	    # drop every cached entry related to the dataset.
137	    invalidate_impact_cache_for_dataset(conn, dataset_name)
138	    return get_schema_version(conn, dataset_name, next_version)

192	def _version_field_definitions(
193	    conn: sqlite3.Connection, version_id: int
194	) -> dict[str, dict]:
195	    """Persisted field definitions of one version keyed by field name."""
196	    rows = conn.execute(
197	        "SELECT name, type, nullable FROM schema_fields WHERE version_id = ?",
198	        (version_id,),
199	    ).fetchall()
200	    return {
201	        row["name"]: {"type": row["type"], "nullable": bool(row["nullable"])}
202	        for row in rows
203	    }

206	def diff_schema_versions(
207	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
208	    dataset_name: str,
209	    from_version: int,
210	    to_version: int,
211	    *,
212	    body: bytes = b"",
213	    query_keys: tuple[str, ...] = (),
214	) -> dict:
215	    """Read-only diff of the persisted field definitions of two versions.
216	
217	    ``from`` is the baseline and ``to`` the target. Only the stored field
218	    definitions (name, type, nullable) are compared; field position is not a
219	    difference. Changes are sorted by field name and each carries ``before``
220	    and ``after`` definitions, null on the side where the field does not
221	    exist. ``compatible`` reports whether the target can take over the
222	    baseline's fields: a removal, a type change or a nullable tightening
223	    (nullable -> not nullable) makes it false; additions and nullable
224	    loosening keep it true.
225	
226	    The endpoint takes no parameters: a non-positive version number is a 422
227	    checked before path resolution, while a non-empty request body or any
228	    query parameter is a 422 raised only after the path dataset and both
229	    versions have resolved, so an unknown dataset/version stays a 404
230	    (mirroring the parameterless audit-report endpoint). Nothing is written.
231	    """
232	    if from_version < 1 or to_version < 1:
233	        raise RequestInvalidError(
234	            "Version numbers in the diff path must be positive integers"
235	        )
236	
237	    dataset = require_dataset(conn, dataset_name)
238	    from_row = _require_schema_version(conn, dataset, from_version)
239	    to_row = _require_schema_version(conn, dataset, to_version)
240	
241	    if body.strip():
242	        raise RequestInvalidError(
243	            "The version diff endpoint does not accept a request body"
244	        )
245	    if query_keys:
246	        raise RequestInvalidError(
247	            "The version diff endpoint does not accept query parameters"
248	        )
249	
250	    from_fields = _version_field_definitions(conn, from_row["id"])
251	    to_fields = _version_field_definitions(conn, to_row["id"])
252	
253	    changes: list[dict] = []
254	    compatible = True
255	    for name in sorted(set(from_fields) | set(to_fields)):
256	        before = from_fields.get(name)
257	        after = to_fields.get(name)
258	        if before == after:
259	            continue
260	        if before is None:
261	            changes.append(
262	                {"field": name, "kind": "added", "before": None, "after": after}
263	            )
264	        elif after is None:
265	            changes.append(
266	                {"field": name, "kind": "removed", "before": before, "after": None}
267	            )
268	            compatible = False
269	        else:
270	            changes.append(
271	                {"field": name, "kind": "changed", "before": before, "after": after}
272	            )
273	            if before["type"] != after["type"] or (
274	                before["nullable"] and not after["nullable"]
275	            ):
276	                compatible = False
277	
278	    return {
279	        "from_version": from_row["version"],
280	        "to_version": to_row["version"],
281	        "compatible": compatible,
282	        "changes": changes,
283	    }

321	def create_lineage_link(
322	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
323	    *,
324	    target_dataset: str,
325	    target_version: int,
326	    target_field: str,
327	    source_dataset: str,
328	    source_version: int,
329	    source_field: str,
330	) -> dict:
331	    target = require_dataset(conn, target_dataset, role="Target dataset")
332	    source = require_dataset(conn, source_dataset, role="Source dataset")
333	
334	    if source["id"] == target["id"]:
335	        raise RequestInvalidError("Source and target datasets must be different")
336	
337	    target_version_id, target_field_id = _require_field(
338	        conn, target, target_version, target_field, role="Target"
339	    )
340	    source_version_id, source_field_id = _require_field(
341	        conn, source, source_version, source_field, role="Source"
342	    )
343	
344	    existing = conn.execute(
345	        "SELECT id FROM lineage_links WHERE target_field_id = ? AND source_field_id = ?",
346	        (target_field_id, source_field_id),
347	    ).fetchone()
348	    if existing is not None:
349	        raise ConflictError(
350	            "This field mapping has already been registered: "
351	            f"'{source_dataset}' v{source_version}.{source_field} -> "
352	            f"'{target_dataset}' v{target_version}.{target_field}"
353	        )
354	
355	    try:
356	        conn.execute(
357	            "INSERT INTO lineage_links ("
358	            "target_dataset_id, target_version_id, target_field_id, "
359	            "source_dataset_id, source_version_id, source_field_id, created_at"
360	            ") VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
361	            (
362	                target["id"],
363	                target_version_id,
364	                target_field_id,
365	                source["id"],
366	                source_version_id,
367	                source_field_id,
368	                utc_now_iso(),
369	            ),
370	        )
371	    except sqlite3.IntegrityError as exc:
372	        raise ConflictError("This field mapping has already been registered") from exc
373	
374	    # The new edge can only extend the impact of fields that reach its source.
375	    _invalidate_impact_cache_for_upstream(
376	        conn, source["name"], source_version, source_field, source_field_id
377	    )
378	
379	    return {
380	        "target_dataset": target["name"],
381	        "target_version": target_version,
382	        "target_field": target_field,
383	        "source": {
384	            "dataset": source["name"],
385	            "version": source_version,
386	            "field": source_field,
387	        },
388	    }

451	def _lineage_forward_edges(
452	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
453	) -> dict[int, list[tuple[int, dict]]]:
454	    """Adjacency of the lineage graph: source field id -> target field refs."""
455	    rows = conn.execute(
456	        """
457	        SELECT  ll.source_field_id AS source_field_id,
458	                ll.target_field_id AS target_field_id,
459	                td.name            AS target_dataset,
460	                tv.version         AS target_version,
461	                tf.name            AS target_field
462	        FROM    lineage_links ll
463	        JOIN    datasets td ON td.id = ll.target_dataset_id
464	        JOIN    schema_versions tv ON tv.id = ll.target_version_id
465	        JOIN    schema_fields tf ON tf.id = ll.target_field_id
466	        """
467	    ).fetchall()
468	    edges: dict[int, list[tuple[int, dict]]] = {}
469	    for row in rows:
470	        ref = {
471	            "dataset": row["target_dataset"],
472	            "version": row["target_version"],
473	            "field": row["target_field"],
474	        }
475	        edges.setdefault(row["source_field_id"], []).append(
476	            (row["target_field_id"], ref)
477	        )
478	    return edges
479	
480	
481	def _compute_impacted(conn: sqlite3.Connection, source_field_id: int) -> list[dict]:
482	    """All fields reachable downstream of the source, deduplicated and sorted.
483	
484	    The source field id is seeded into the visited set, so cycles terminate
485	    and the source itself never appears in the result.
486	    """
487	    edges = _lineage_forward_edges(conn)
488	    visited = {source_field_id}
489	    impacted: dict[tuple[str, int, str], dict] = {}
490	    queue = [source_field_id]
491	    while queue:
492	        current = queue.pop()
493	        for target_field_id, ref in edges.get(current, ()):
494	            if target_field_id in visited:
495	                continue
496	            visited.add(target_field_id)
497	            impacted[(ref["dataset"], ref["version"], ref["field"])] = ref
498	            queue.append(target_field_id)
499	    return [impacted[key] for key in sorted(impacted)]
500

507	        "WHERE source_dataset = ? AND source_version = ? AND source_field = ?",
508	        (dataset, version, field),
509	    ).fetchone()

513	def _impact_cache_store(
514	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
515	    dataset: str,
516	    version: int,
517	    field: str,
518	    impacted: list[dict],
519	) -> None:

521	        "DELETE FROM lineage_impact_cache "
522	        "WHERE source_dataset = ? AND source_version = ? AND source_field = ?",
523	        (dataset, version, field),
524	    )

552	def _invalidate_impact_cache_for_upstream(
553	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
554	    source_dataset: str,
555	    source_version: int,
556	    source_field: str,
557	    source_field_id: int,
558	) -> None:
559	    """Invalidate cached impacts of the new link's source and its upstream.
560	
561	    A new mapping ``source -> target`` only changes the impact result of
562	    fields that can reach ``source`` (``source`` itself included), so exactly
563	    those cached entries are dropped; unrelated entries are kept. The reverse
564	    walk runs after the link was inserted so cycles are covered too.
565	    """
566	    rows = conn.execute(
567	        """
568	        SELECT  ll.target_field_id AS target_field_id,
569	                ll.source_field_id AS source_field_id,
570	                sd.name            AS source_dataset,
571	                sv.version         AS source_version,
572	                sf.name            AS source_field
573	        FROM    lineage_links ll
574	        JOIN    datasets sd ON sd.id = ll.source_dataset_id
575	        JOIN    schema_versions sv ON sv.id = ll.source_version_id
576	        JOIN    schema_fields sf ON sf.id = ll.source_field_id
577	        """
578	    ).fetchall()
579	    reverse: dict[int, list[sqlite3.Row]] = {}
580	    for row in rows:
581	        reverse.setdefault(row["target_field_id"], []).append(row)
582	
583	    visited = {source_field_id}
584	    upstream = {(source_dataset, source_version, source_field)}
585	    queue = [source_field_id]
586	    while queue:
587	        current = queue.pop()
588	        for row in reverse.get(current, ()):
589	            if row["source_field_id"] in visited:
590	                continue
591	            visited.add(row["source_field_id"])
592	            upstream.add(
593	                (row["source_dataset"], row["source_version"], row["source_field"])
594	            )
595	            queue.append(row["source_field_id"])
596	
597	    conn.executemany(
598	        "DELETE FROM lineage_impact_cache "
599	        "WHERE source_dataset = ? AND source_version = ? AND source_field = ?",
600	        sorted(upstream),
601	    )
602

604	def get_lineage_impact(
605	    conn: sqlite3.Connection, dataset_name: str, version: int, field: str
606	) -> dict:
607	    dataset = require_dataset(conn, dataset_name)
608	    _, field_id = _require_field(conn, dataset, version, field, role="Source")
609	
610	    impacted = _impact_cache_lookup(conn, dataset["name"], version, field)
611	    if impacted is None:
612	        impacted = _compute_impacted(conn, field_id)
613	        _impact_cache_store(conn, dataset["name"], version, field, impacted)
614	
615	    return {
616	        "source": {"dataset": dataset["name"], "version": version, "field": field},
617	        "impacted": impacted,
618	    }

651	def _is_finite_number(value: Any) -> bool:
652	    # bool is a subclass of int; a boolean is not a numeric value here.
653	    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (int, float)):
654	        return False
655	    return math.isfinite(value)

658	def _validate_rule_params(
659	    kind: str, params: dict[str, Any], field_names: set[str]
660	) -> None:
661	    """Validate rule parameters structurally (422) and against the schema (404)."""
662	
663	    def require_existing_field(field_name: Any) -> str:
664	        if not isinstance(field_name, str) or not field_name:
665	            raise RequestInvalidError(
666	                f"Rule kind '{kind}' requires a non-empty 'field' parameter"
667	            )
668	        if field_name not in field_names:
669	            raise NotFoundError(f"Field '{field_name}' does not exist in this version")
670	        return field_name
671	
672	    if kind == "not_null":
673	        require_existing_field(params.get("field"))
674	        return
675	
676	    if kind == "numeric_range":
677	        field_name = require_existing_field(params.get("field"))
678	        minimum = params.get("min")
679	        maximum = params.get("max")
680	        if not _is_finite_number(minimum) or not _is_finite_number(maximum):
681	            raise RequestInvalidError(
682	                f"Rule on field '{field_name}' requires finite numeric 'min' and 'max'"
683	            )
684	        if minimum > maximum:
685	            raise RequestInvalidError(
686	                f"Rule on field '{field_name}' requires min <= max"
687	            )
688	        return
689	
690	    if kind == "unique":
691	        fields = params.get("fields")
692	        if not isinstance(fields, list) or not fields:
693	            raise RequestInvalidError(
694	                "Rule kind 'unique' requires a non-empty 'fields' list"
695	            )
696	        if not all(isinstance(name, str) and name for name in fields):
697	            raise RequestInvalidError(
698	                "Rule kind 'unique' requires 'fields' to contain non-empty field names"
699	            )
700	        if len(set(fields)) != len(fields):
701	            raise RequestInvalidError(
702	                "Rule kind 'unique' requires 'fields' to contain no duplicates"
703	            )
704	        unknown = [name for name in fields if name not in field_names]
705	        if unknown:
706	            raise NotFoundError(
707	                f"Field '{unknown[0]}' does not exist in this version"
708	            )
709	        return

811	def _row_violates_not_null(row: dict[str, Any], field: str) -> bool:
812	    return field not in row or row[field] is None
813	
814	
815	def _row_violates_numeric_range(
816	    row: dict[str, Any], field: str, minimum: float, maximum: float
817	) -> bool:
818	    if field not in row:
819	        return True
820	    value = row[field]
821	    if value is None or not _is_finite_number(value):
822	        return True
823	    return value < minimum or value > maximum

826	def _row_violates_unique(row: dict[str, Any], fields: list[str]) -> tuple:
827	    return tuple(None if name not in row else row[name] for name in fields)

830	def _json_combo_key(combo: tuple) -> str:
831	    # Values are already JSON-decoded scalars (or nested arrays/objects); use
832	    # JSON text so that, e.g., the number 1 and the string "1" never compare
833	    # equal and nested objects with reordered keys still match.
834	    return json.dumps(combo, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))

837	def evaluate_quality_rules(
838	    conn: sqlite3.Connection, dataset_name: str, version_number: int, rows: list[dict]
839	) -> dict:
840	    dataset = require_dataset(conn, dataset_name)
841	    version_row = _require_schema_version(conn, dataset, version_number)
842	
843	    rule_rows = conn.execute(
844	        "SELECT id, name, kind, params, enabled "
845	        "FROM quality_rules WHERE version_id = ? AND enabled = 1 ORDER BY id",
846	        (version_row["id"],),
847	    ).fetchall()
848	
849	    results: list[dict] = []
850	    for rule_row in rule_rows:
851	        params = json.loads(rule_row["params"])
852	        kind = rule_row["kind"]
853	        violations: list[int] = []
854	
855	        if kind == "not_null":
856	            field = params["field"]
857	            violations = [
858	                index
859	                for index, row in enumerate(rows)
860	                if _row_violates_not_null(row, field)
861	            ]
862	        elif kind == "numeric_range":
863	            field = params["field"]
864	            violations = [
865	                index
866	                for index, row in enumerate(rows)
867	                if _row_violates_numeric_range(
868	                    row, field, params["min"], params["max"]
869	                )
870	            ]
871	        elif kind == "unique":
872	            fields = params["fields"]
873	            seen: dict[str, int] = {}
874	            duplicated: set[int] = set()
875	            for index, row in enumerate(rows):
876	                combo = _row_violates_unique(row, fields)
877	                key = _json_combo_key(combo)
878	                if key in seen:
879	                    duplicated.add(seen[key])
880	                    duplicated.add(index)
881	                else:
882	                    seen[key] = index
883	            violations = sorted(duplicated)
884	
885	        results.append(
886	            {
887	                "rule_id": rule_row["id"],
888	                "name": rule_row["name"],
889	                "passed": not violations,
890	                "violations": violations,
891	            }
892	        )
893	
894	    # Every successful evaluation appends an immutable summary to the history
895	    # (an empty submission is recorded too, with zero violations). A rejected
896	    # or failed evaluation raises above and leaves no record.
897	    _record_quality_rule_evaluation(
898	        conn,
899	        version_row["id"],
900	        row_count=len(rows),
901	        violation_row_count=len(
902	            {index for result in results for index in result["violations"]}
903	        ),
904	        results=results,
905	    )
906	
907	    return {
908	        "dataset": dataset["name"],
909	        "version": version_row["version"],
910	        "results": results,
911	    }

914	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
915	# Quality rule evaluation history (append-only) and read-only diff
916	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
917	
918	
919	# Serializes read-tail -> append within this process so concurrent evaluations
920	# never compute the same sequence. SQLite's UNIQUE(version_id, sequence)
921	# constraint is the hard guard against writers in other processes; such a
922	# collision is resolved with a bounded re-read-and-retry (mirrors the audit
923	# record append).
924	_evaluation_append_locks: dict[int, threading.Lock] = {}
925	_evaluation_append_locks_guard = threading.Lock()
926	
927	# Bound on re-read-and-retry attempts when a writer in another process wins the
928	# race for the same (version_id, sequence).
929	_EVALUATION_APPEND_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 100

941	def _record_quality_rule_evaluation(
942	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
943	    version_id: int,
944	    *,
945	    row_count: int,
946	    violation_row_count: int,
947	    results: list[dict],
948	) -> None:
949	    """Append one evaluation summary as the next sequence of the version.
950	
951	    The per-version lock makes read-tail -> append atomic within this process
952	    (FastAPI runs this synchronous endpoint in one process's threadpool). The
953	    UNIQUE(version_id, sequence) constraint is the hard cross-process guard; a
954	    writer that loses a race against another process retries with the new tail
955	    instead of failing the request.
956	    """
957	    stored_results = json.dumps(results)
958	    with _evaluation_append_lock(version_id):
959	        for attempt in range(_EVALUATION_APPEND_MAX_ATTEMPTS):
960	            tail = conn.execute(
961	                "SELECT MAX(sequence) AS max_sequence "
962	                "FROM quality_rule_evaluations WHERE version_id = ?",
963	                (version_id,),
964	            ).fetchone()
965	            sequence = (tail["max_sequence"] or 0) + 1
966	            try:
967	                conn.execute(
968	                    "INSERT INTO quality_rule_evaluations ("
969	                    "version_id, sequence, row_count, violation_row_count, "
970	                    "results, created_at"
971	                    ") VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
972	                    (
973	                        version_id,
974	                        sequence,
975	                        row_count,
976	                        violation_row_count,
977	                        stored_results,
978	                        utc_now_iso(),
979	                    ),
980	                )
981	                return
982	            except sqlite3.IntegrityError:
983	                # Another process inserted the same sequence first. End the
984	                # current (pinned) transaction so the re-read establishes a new
985	                # snapshot that includes the competing commit, then retry.
986	                if attempt + 1 == _EVALUATION_APPEND_MAX_ATTEMPTS:
987	                    conn.rollback()
988	                    raise ConflictError(
989	                        "Too many concurrent evaluation writes; retry the request"
990	                    )
991	                conn.rollback()
992	                continue

1062	def diff_quality_rule_evaluations(
1063	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
1064	    dataset_name: str,
1065	    version_number: int,
1066	    *,
1067	    body: bytes = b"",
1068	    query_keys: tuple[str, ...] = (),
1069	) -> dict:
1070	    """Read-only diff between the two most recent evaluations of one version.
1071	
1072	    The latest recorded evaluation (``to``) is compared against its immediate
1073	    predecessor (``from``) using exactly the results each of them recorded;
1074	    the persisted rule definitions and submitted rows of the two evaluations
1075	    are all that is consulted. Row positions are the 0-based indices each
1076	    evaluation reported. A rule missing from one side (disabled or not yet
1077	    created between the two evaluations) keeps a null side, and its row-level
1078	    diff fields are null as well, so a missing side stays distinguishable from
1079	    a present side with zero violations. With fewer than two recorded
1080	    evaluations the result is explicitly empty (null sequences, empty lists),
1081	    never an error. Nothing is written.
1082	    """
1083	    dataset, version_row = _require_evaluation_path(
1084	        conn, dataset_name, version_number, body=body, query_keys=query_keys,
1085	        endpoint="evaluation diff",
1086	    )
1087	    rows = conn.execute(
1088	        "SELECT * FROM quality_rule_evaluations WHERE version_id = ? "
1089	        "ORDER BY sequence DESC LIMIT 2",
1090	        (version_row["id"],),
1091	    ).fetchall()
1092	
1093	    empty = {
1094	        "dataset": dataset["name"],
1095	        "version": version_row["version"],
1096	        "from_sequence": None,
1097	        "to_sequence": None,
1098	        "added_violation_rows": [],
1099	        "removed_violation_rows": [],
1100	        "rules": [],
1101	    }
1102	    if len(rows) < 2:
1103	        return empty
1104	
1105	    to_row, from_row = rows[0], rows[1]
1106	    before_results = {r["rule_id"]: r for r in json.loads(from_row["results"])}
1107	    after_results = {r["rule_id"]: r for r in json.loads(to_row["results"])}
1108	
1109	    rule_diffs: list[dict] = []
1110	    for rule_id in sorted(set(before_results) | set(after_results)):
1111	        before = before_results.get(rule_id)
1112	        after = after_results.get(rule_id)
1113	        if before is not None and after is not None:
1114	            before_set = set(before["violations"])
1115	            after_set = set(after["violations"])
1116	            added: list[int] | None = sorted(after_set - before_set)
1117	            removed: list[int] | None = sorted(before_set - after_set)
1118	            delta: int | None = len(after["violations"]) - len(before["violations"])
1119	        else:
1120	            added = removed = delta = None
1121	        rule_diffs.append(
1122	            {
1123	                "rule_id": rule_id,
1124	                "name": (after if after is not None else before)["name"],
1125	                "before": (
1126	                    None
1127	                    if before is None
1128	                    else {
1129	                        "violation_count": len(before["violations"]),
1130	                        "violations": before["violations"],
1131	                    }
1132	                ),
1133	                "after": (
1134	                    None
1135	                    if after is None
1136	                    else {
1137	                        "violation_count": len(after["violations"]),
1138	                        "violations": after["violations"],
1139	                    }
1140	                ),
1141	                "added_violations": added,
1142	                "removed_violations": removed,
1143	                "violation_count_delta": delta,
1144	            }
1145	        )
1146	
1147	    before_rows = {
1148	        index for result in before_results.values() for index in result["violations"]
1149	    }
1150	    after_rows = {
1151	        index for result in after_results.values() for index in result["violations"]
1152	    }
1153	
1154	    return {
1155	        "dataset": dataset["name"],
1156	        "version": version_row["version"],
1157	        "from_sequence": from_row["sequence"],
1158	        "to_sequence": to_row["sequence"],
1159	        "added_violation_rows": sorted(after_rows - before_rows),
1160	        "removed_violation_rows": sorted(before_rows - after_rows),
1161	        "rules": rule_diffs,
1162	    }

1286	def _anomaly_candidates(
1287	    history_rows: list[sqlite3.Row], config_row: sqlite3.Row
1288	) -> list[tuple[str, int, int | None, int]]:
1289	    """All anomalies of one scan, in deterministic insertion order.
1290	
1291	    Row-limit and rule-limit records are emitted per evaluation in history
1292	    sequence order (rule-limit records ordered by rule id within one
1293	    evaluation); the trend record, which always points at the final
1294	    evaluation, comes last.
1295	    """
1296	    candidates: list[tuple[str, int, int | None, int]] = []
1297	    row_limit = config_row["violation_row_limit"]
1298	    rule_limit = config_row["rule_violation_limit"]
1299	    for history_row in history_rows:
1300	        sequence = history_row["sequence"]
1301	        violation_row_count = history_row["violation_row_count"]
1302	        if violation_row_count > row_limit:
1303	            candidates.append(("row_limit", sequence, None, violation_row_count))
1304	        results = json.loads(history_row["results"])
1305	        for result in sorted(results, key=lambda item: item["rule_id"]):
1306	            violation_count = len(result["violations"])
1307	            if violation_count > rule_limit:
1308	                candidates.append(
1309	                    ("rule_limit", sequence, result["rule_id"], violation_count)
1310	                )
1311	
1312	    # Trend: the violation row counts of adjacent evaluations must strictly
1313	    # increase step by step; when the consecutive increase count at the tail
1314	    # of the history reaches the configured step count, the final evaluation
1315	    # of the increasing sequence is anomalous. A shorter run or any decline
1316	    # (or plateau) at the tail produces no trend record.
1317	    counts = [row["violation_row_count"] for row in history_rows]
1318	    trailing_increases = 0
1319	    for previous, current in zip(counts, counts[1:]):
1320	        trailing_increases = trailing_increases + 1 if current > previous else 0
1321	    if trailing_increases >= config_row["consecutive_worsening_steps"]:
1322	        candidates.append(("trend", history_rows[-1]["sequence"], None, counts[-1]))
1323	    return candidates

1326	def _scan_anomalies_once(conn: sqlite3.Connection, version_id: int) -> list[dict]:
1327	    config_row = conn.execute(
1328	        "SELECT * FROM quality_anomaly_detection_configs WHERE version_id = ?",
1329	        (version_id,),
1330	    ).fetchone()
1331	    if config_row is None:
1332	        raise ConflictError(
1333	            "No anomaly detection config is registered for this version; "
1334	            "register one before scanning"
1335	        )
1336	
1337	    history_rows = conn.execute(
1338	        "SELECT * FROM quality_rule_evaluations WHERE version_id = ? "
1339	        "ORDER BY sequence ASC",
1340	        (version_id,),
1341	    ).fetchall()
1342	    if not history_rows:
1343	        return []
1344	
1345	    existing = {
1346	        (
1347	            row["kind"],
1348	            row["sequence"],
1349	            row["rule_id"] if row["rule_id"] is not None else 0,
1350	        )
1351	        for row in conn.execute(
1352	            "SELECT kind, sequence, rule_id FROM quality_anomaly_records "
1353	            "WHERE version_id = ?",
1354	            (version_id,),
1355	        ).fetchall()
1356	    }
1357	
1358	    inserted_ids: list[int] = []
1359	    for kind, sequence, rule_id, violation_count in _anomaly_candidates(
1360	        history_rows, config_row
1361	    ):
1362	        key = (kind, sequence, rule_id if rule_id is not None else 0)
1363	        if key in existing:
1364	            continue
1365	        cursor = conn.execute(
1366	            "INSERT INTO quality_anomaly_records ("
1367	            "version_id, kind, sequence, rule_id, violation_count, created_at"
1368	            ") VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
1369	            (version_id, kind, sequence, rule_id, violation_count, utc_now_iso()),
1370	        )
1371	        existing.add(key)
1372	        inserted_ids.append(cursor.lastrowid)
1373	
1374	    if not inserted_ids:
1375	        return []
1376	    placeholders = ", ".join("?" for _ in inserted_ids)
1377	    rows = conn.execute(
1378	        f"SELECT * FROM quality_anomaly_records WHERE id IN ({placeholders}) "
1379	        "ORDER BY id ASC",
1380	        inserted_ids,
1381	    ).fetchall()
1382	    return [_anomaly_row_to_dict(row) for row in rows]

1385	def scan_quality_anomalies(
1386	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
1387	    dataset_name: str,
1388	    version_number: int,
1389	    *,
1390	    body: bytes = b"",
1391	    query_keys: tuple[str, ...] = (),
1392	) -> list[dict]:
1393	    """Run one anomaly detection pass over the persisted evaluation history.
1394	
1395	    Only the persisted evaluation summaries and the version's registered
1396	    config are consulted; rule definitions are never written. A record already
1397	    stored (same kind, history sequence and rule id) is never duplicated, so a
1398	    repeated scan only persists — and returns — the anomalies that newly
1399	    appear. The response holds exactly the records this scan inserted, ordered
1400	    by id. Scanning without a registered config is a 409; an empty history is
1401	    a successful scan that writes nothing.
1402	    """
1403	    dataset, version_row = _require_evaluation_path(
1404	        conn,
1405	        dataset_name,
1406	        version_number,
1407	        body=body,
1408	        query_keys=query_keys,
1409	        endpoint="anomaly scan",
1410	    )
1411	    version_id = version_row["id"]
1412	    with _anomaly_scan_lock(version_id):
1413	        for attempt in range(_ANOMALY_SCAN_MAX_ATTEMPTS):
1414	            try:
1415	                return _scan_anomalies_once(conn, version_id)
1416	            except sqlite3.IntegrityError:
1417	                # Another process committed records between this scan's read
1418	                # of the existing records and its inserts. End the current
1419	                # (pinned) transaction so the re-read sees that commit, then
1420	                # only insert what is still missing (mirrors the evaluation
1421	                # append retry).
1422	                if attempt + 1 == _ANOMALY_SCAN_MAX_ATTEMPTS:
1423	                    conn.rollback()
1424	                    raise ConflictError(
1425	                        "Too many concurrent anomaly scans; retry the request"
1426	                    )
1427	                conn.rollback()
1428	                continue

# Append-only audit of privacy-view masking hits. One record is written per
# field actually masked by a view request; ``sequence`` numbers the records of
# one version in write order.
class PrivacyViewAuditRecord(BaseModel):
    sequence: int
    field: str
    policy_id: int
    role: str
    masking: PrivacyMasking
    created_at: str


# One record per successful privacy-view request, independent of how many
# values it masked. ``sequence`` numbers the records of one version in write
# order; ``row_count`` is the number of submitted rows and ``masked_count``
# the number of masking-hit records the same view wrote, so the two logs
# cross-check.
class PrivacyViewAccessRecord(BaseModel):
    sequence: int
    role: str
    row_count: int
    masked_count: int
    created_at: str


# Read-only roll-up of the masking-hit records: one group per distinct
# (field, policy, role, masking) combination, with the number of hits and the
# timestamps of the group's earliest and latest written records. Recomputed
# from the persisted records on every read; nothing is cached or written.
class PrivacyViewAuditSummaryGroup(BaseModel):
    field: str
    policy_id: int
    role: str
    masking: PrivacyMasking
    hit_count: int
    first_hit_at: str
    last_hit_at: str


class PrivacyViewAuditSummaryResponse(BaseModel):
    dataset: str
    version: int
    groups: list[PrivacyViewAuditSummaryGroup]


# Read-only day-over-day comparison of the masking-hit records: the records of
# the two most recent UTC calendar days are grouped by
# (field, policy, role, masking) and each side reports its hit count and the
# timestamps of the group's earliest and latest records of that day. A group
# present on only one side keeps a null ``before``/``after`` for the missing

# or written.

    hit_count: int
    first_hit_at: str
    last_hit_at: str

    role: str
    masking: PrivacyMasking
    kind: Literal["added", "removed", "changed"]
    before: PrivacyViewAuditDiffSide | None
    after: PrivacyViewAuditDiffSide | None
    hit_count_delta: int


class PrivacyViewAuditDiffResponse(BaseModel):
    from_period: str | None
    to_period: str | None
    groups: list[PrivacyViewAuditDiffGroup]


# Read-only per-day reconciliation of the access records against the

    view_count: int
    masked_count: int
    hit_count: int
    consistent: bool

    masked_count: int
    hit_count: int

_PRIVACY_VIEW_AUDIT_SEARCH_PARAMETERS: frozenset[str] = frozenset(
    {"role", "field", "start", "end"}

def _parse_audit_interval_timestamp(raw: str, param: str) -> datetime:
    """Parse one bound of the search write-time interval.

    The bound must be an ISO-8601 date-time carrying a timezone designator
    (offset or 'Z'); anything else (including an empty value) is a 422.
    """
    try:
        parsed = datetime.fromisoformat(raw)
    except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
        raise RequestInvalidError(
            f"Query parameter '{param}' must be an ISO-8601 date-time"
        ) from exc
    if parsed.tzinfo is None or parsed.utcoffset() is None:
        raise RequestInvalidError(
            f"Query parameter '{param}' must include a timezone"
        )
    return parsed


def search_privacy_view_audit_records(
    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
    dataset_name: str,
    version_number: int,
    *,
    role: str | None = None,
    field: str | None = None,
    start: str | None = None,
    end: str | None = None,
    body: bytes = b"",
    query_keys: tuple[str, ...] = (),
) -> list[dict]:
    """Masking-hit records of a version matching optional read-only filters.

    The filters are all optional and combine with AND: ``role`` and ``field``
    match the stored values exactly apart from letter case (no trimming, no
    substring matching); ``start``/``end`` are timezone-aware ISO-8601 bounds
    of a closed interval on the record write time, either one being omissible.
    Matched records keep the full-list field shape and sequence-ascending
    order. No match yields an empty list; an interval whose start is later
    than its end is a 422.

    Read-only: the path dataset/version resolves first (404); a non-empty
    request body, an unknown query parameter, an unparseable or timezone-less
    bound, or a reversed interval is a 422 checked afterwards, mirroring the
    full record list. Nothing is written.
    """
    dataset = require_dataset(conn, dataset_name)
    version_row = _require_schema_version(conn, dataset, version_number)

    if body.strip():
        raise RequestInvalidError(
            "The privacy view audit records search endpoint does not accept "
            "a request body"
        )
    unknown_keys = sorted(set(query_keys) - _PRIVACY_VIEW_AUDIT_SEARCH_PARAMETERS)
    if unknown_keys:
        raise RequestInvalidError(
            "Unknown query parameter(s): " + ", ".join(unknown_keys)
        )

    start_at = (
        _parse_audit_interval_timestamp(start, "start")
        if start is not None
        else None
    )
    end_at = (
        _parse_audit_interval_timestamp(end, "end") if end is not None else None
    )
    if start_at is not None and end_at is not None and start_at > end_at:
        raise RequestInvalidError(
            "Query parameter 'start' must not be later than 'end'"
        )

    rows = conn.execute(
        "SELECT * FROM privacy_view_audit_records WHERE version_id = ? "
        "ORDER BY sequence ASC",
        (version_row["id"],),
    ).fetchall()

    role_match = role.lower() if role is not None else None
    field_match = field.lower() if field is not None else None
    results: list[dict] = []
    for row in rows:
        if role_match is not None and row["role"].lower() != role_match:
            continue
        if field_match is not None and row["field"].lower() != field_match:
            continue
        if start_at is not None or end_at is not None:
            written_at = datetime.fromisoformat(row["created_at"])
            if start_at is not None and written_at < start_at:
                continue
            if end_at is not None and written_at > end_at:
                continue
        results.append(_privacy_view_audit_row_to_dict(row))
    return results


def summarize_privacy_view_audit_records(
    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
    dataset_name: str,
    version_number: int,
    *,
    body: bytes = b"",
    query_keys: tuple[str, ...] = (),
) -> dict:
    """Read-only compliance summary of the masking-hit records of a version.

    The records are grouped by ``(field, policy_id, role, masking)``; each
    group reports its record count (one record is one hit, never row- or
    field-weighted) and the earliest/latest ``created_at`` among its records.
    Groups sort by field, then policy id, role and masking, all ascending. The
    summary is recomputed from the persisted records on every call: it caches
    nothing and writes nothing.

    Like the record list, the path dataset/version resolves first (404); a
    non-empty request body or any query parameter is a 422 checked afterwards.
    A version without records yields an empty group list.
    """
    dataset = require_dataset(conn, dataset_name)
    version_row = _require_schema_version(conn, dataset, version_number)

    if body.strip():
        raise RequestInvalidError(
            "The privacy view audit summary endpoint does not accept a "
            "request body"
        )
    if query_keys:
        raise RequestInvalidError(
            "The privacy view audit summary endpoint does not accept query "
            "parameters"
        )

    rows = conn.execute(
        "SELECT field, policy_id, role, masking, "
        "COUNT(*) AS hit_count, "
        "MIN(created_at) AS first_hit_at, "
        "MAX(created_at) AS last_hit_at "
        "FROM privacy_view_audit_records WHERE version_id = ? "
        "GROUP BY field, policy_id, role, masking "
        "ORDER BY field ASC, policy_id ASC, role ASC, masking ASC",
        (version_row["id"],),
    ).fetchall()
    groups = [
        {
            "field": row["field"],
            "policy_id": row["policy_id"],
            "role": row["role"],
            "masking": row["masking"],
            "hit_count": row["hit_count"],
            "first_hit_at": row["first_hit_at"],
            "last_hit_at": row["last_hit_at"],
        }
        for row in rows
    ]
    return {
        "dataset": dataset["name"],
        "version": version_row["version"],
        "groups": groups,
    }


def diff_privacy_view_audit_records(
    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
    dataset_name: str,
    version_number: int,
    *,
    body: bytes = b"",
    query_keys: tuple[str, ...] = (),
) -> dict:
    """Read-only day-over-day diff of the masking-hit records of a version.

    Records are bucketed by the UTC calendar day of their ``created_at`` write
    time; the two most recent days with records are compared, the earlier day
    being the baseline (``from_period``) and the later one the target
    (``to_period``). Each side is grouped by ``(field, policy_id, role,
    masking)``; a group reports its record count (one record is one hit) and
    the earliest/latest ``created_at`` of its records of that day. A group
    present on both days is ``changed``; one only on the target day is
    ``added`` and one only on the baseline day is ``removed``. The missing
    side of a one-sided group is null (never omitted) and counts as zero in
    ``hit_count_delta`` (target minus baseline). Groups sort by field, policy
    id, role and masking, all ascending, never relying on database order.

    With fewer than two calendar days of records the comparison is explicitly
    empty (null periods, empty group list), never an error. The diff is
    recomputed from the persisted records on every call: it caches nothing,
    writes nothing and never touches the hit records.

    Like the record list, the path dataset/version resolves first (404); a
    non-empty request body or any query parameter is a 422 checked afterwards.
    """
    dataset = require_dataset(conn, dataset_name)
    version_row = _require_schema_version(conn, dataset, version_number)

    if body.strip():
        raise RequestInvalidError(
            "The privacy view audit diff endpoint does not accept a "
            "request body"
        )
    if query_keys:
        raise RequestInvalidError(
            "The privacy view audit diff endpoint does not accept query "
            "parameters"
        )

    day_rows = conn.execute(
        "SELECT DISTINCT date(created_at) AS day "
        "FROM privacy_view_audit_records WHERE version_id = ? "
        "ORDER BY day DESC LIMIT 2",
        (version_row["id"],),
    ).fetchall()

    if len(day_rows) < 2:
        return {"from_period": None, "to_period": None, "groups": []}

    to_period = day_rows[0]["day"]
    from_period = day_rows[1]["day"]

    rows = conn.execute(
        "SELECT field, policy_id, role, masking, date(created_at) AS day, "
        "COUNT(*) AS hit_count, "
        "MIN(created_at) AS first_hit_at, "
        "MAX(created_at) AS last_hit_at "
        "FROM privacy_view_audit_records "
        "WHERE version_id = ? AND date(created_at) IN (?, ?) "
        "GROUP BY field, policy_id, role, masking, day",
        (version_row["id"], from_period, to_period),
    ).fetchall()

    def side(row: sqlite3.Row) -> dict:
        return {
            "hit_count": row["hit_count"],
            "first_hit_at": row["first_hit_at"],
            "last_hit_at": row["last_hit_at"],
        }

    by_key: dict[tuple, dict[str, dict | None]] = {}
    for row in rows:
        key = (row["field"], row["policy_id"], row["role"], row["masking"])
        entry = by_key.setdefault(key, {"before": None, "after": None})
        entry["before" if row["day"] == from_period else "after"] = side(row)

    groups: list[dict] = []
    for key in sorted(by_key):
        field, policy_id, role, masking = key
        before = by_key[key]["before"]
        after = by_key[key]["after"]
        if before is None:
            kind = "added"
        elif after is None:
            kind = "removed"
        else:
            kind = "changed"
        groups.append(
            {
                "field": field,
                "policy_id": policy_id,
                "role": role,
                "masking": masking,
                "kind": kind,
                "before": before,
                "after": after,
                "hit_count_delta": (after or {"hit_count": 0})["hit_count"]
                - (before or {"hit_count": 0})["hit_count"],
            }
        )

    return {"from_period": from_period, "to_period": to_period, "groups": groups}


def reconcile_privacy_view_audit_records(
    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
    dataset_name: str,
    version_number: int,
    *,
    body: bytes = b"",
    query_keys: tuple[str, ...] = (),
) -> dict:
    """Read-only per-day reconciliation of access records against hit records.

    Both logs are bucketed by the UTC calendar day of their ``created_at``
    write time. Each day with records on either side reports ``view_count``
    (access records written that day), ``masked_count`` (the masked-value
    counts of those access records summed) and ``hit_count`` (masking-hit
    records written that day); a side without records on that day counts as
    zero. ``consistent`` is true exactly when ``masked_count`` equals
    ``hit_count`` — the access log's masked-value total cross-checks the hit
    log. Days sort ascending by date, never relying on database order; days
    without any record on either side do not appear. ``totals`` sums the
    same three counts over the whole version, so it always equals the
    per-day entries added together (all zero when there are no records).

    The reconciliation is recomputed from the persisted records on every
    call: it caches nothing, writes nothing and never touches either log.
    Like the record list, the path dataset/version resolves first (404); a
    non-empty request body or any query parameter is a 422 checked
    afterwards.
    """
    dataset = require_dataset(conn, dataset_name)
    version_row = _require_schema_version(conn, dataset, version_number)

    if body.strip():
        raise RequestInvalidError(
            "The privacy view audit reconcile endpoint does not accept a "
            "request body"
        )
    if query_keys:
        raise RequestInvalidError(
            "The privacy view audit reconcile endpoint does not accept query "
            "parameters"
        )

    access_rows = conn.execute(
        "SELECT date(created_at) AS day, COUNT(*) AS view_count, "
        "SUM(masked_count) AS masked_count "
        "FROM privacy_view_access_records WHERE version_id = ? "
        "GROUP BY day",
        (version_row["id"],),
    ).fetchall()
    hit_rows = conn.execute(
        "SELECT date(created_at) AS day, COUNT(*) AS hit_count "
        "FROM privacy_view_audit_records WHERE version_id = ? "
        "GROUP BY day",
        (version_row["id"],),
    ).fetchall()

    by_day: dict[str, dict[str, int]] = {}
    for row in access_rows:
        entry = by_day.setdefault(
            row["day"], {"view_count": 0, "masked_count": 0, "hit_count": 0}
        )
        entry["view_count"] = row["view_count"]
        entry["masked_count"] = row["masked_count"]
    for row in hit_rows:
        entry = by_day.setdefault(
            row["day"], {"view_count": 0, "masked_count": 0, "hit_count": 0}
        )
        entry["hit_count"] = row["hit_count"]

    days = [
        {
            "day": day,
            "view_count": entry["view_count"],
            "masked_count": entry["masked_count"],
            "hit_count": entry["hit_count"],
            "consistent": entry["masked_count"] == entry["hit_count"],
        }
        for day, entry in sorted(by_day.items())
    ]
    totals = {
        "view_count": sum(entry["view_count"] for entry in days),
        "masked_count": sum(entry["masked_count"] for entry in days),
        "hit_count": sum(entry["hit_count"] for entry in days),
    }
    return {
        "dataset": dataset["name"],
        "version": version_row["version"],
        "days": days,
        "totals": totals,
    }

# Sensitive-field identification (candidate annotation only)

# Sensitive words matched case-insensitively as substrings of the field name,
# in evidence-emission order.
SENSITIVE_WORDS: tuple[str, ...] = (
    "email",
    "phone",
    "id_card",
    "password",
    "token",
    "birth",
)

# Phone numbers are matched against ASCII 0-9 only (str.isdigit() also accepts
# e.g. superscript or full-width Unicode digits).
_ASCII_DIGITS = re.compile(r"[0-9]+\Z")


def _sensitive_name_evidence(field_name: str) -> list[str]:
    """Name-hit kinds for one field name, in sensitive-word order."""
    lowered = field_name.lower()
    return [f"name:{word}" for word in SENSITIVE_WORDS if word in lowered]


def _text_sample_hits(text: str) -> set[str]:
    """Sample-hit kinds for one string value.

    Email: exactly one ``@`` with non-empty text on both sides and a dot in the
    domain. Phone: an 11-digit ASCII decimal string starting with ``1``. The
    two formats are disjoint (an email must contain ``@``).
    """
    hits: set[str] = set()
    if text.count("@") == 1:
        local, _, domain = text.partition("@")
        if local and domain and "." in domain:
            hits.add("sample:email")
    if len(text) == 11 and text[0] == "1" and _ASCII_DIGITS.match(text):
        hits.add("sample:phone")
    return hits


def _sensitive_sample_evidence(samples: list[Any]) -> list[str]:
    """Sample-hit kinds across all samples; only string values participate."""
    hits: set[str] = set()
    for sample in samples:
        if isinstance(sample, str):
            hits |= _text_sample_hits(sample)
    return [
        kind for kind in ("sample:email", "sample:phone") if kind in hits
    ]


def _identify_sensitive(
    field_name: str, field_type: str, samples: list[Any]
) -> tuple[list[str], str]:
    """Combine name and sample evidence for one field.

    Name evidence is independent of the declared type. Sample evidence is only
    computed for fields declared ``string``: every other declared type is
    matched by name only even when a sample looks like an email. Evidence is
    name hits followed by sample hits (each group de-duplicated). Confidence is
    ``high`` when both sides hit, ``medium`` for samples only, ``low`` for the
    name only and ``none`` when neither hits (the record is still generated).
    """
    name_evidence = _sensitive_name_evidence(field_name)
    sample_evidence = (
        _sensitive_sample_evidence(samples) if field_type == "string" else []
    )
    evidence = name_evidence + sample_evidence

"""Pydantic models for the dataset, schema-version and lineage APIs."""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any, Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, StrictBool, StrictFloat, StrictInt, StrictStr

    name: str = Field(description="Unique, non-empty dataset name")
    description: str = Field(default="", description="Optional human description")


class Dataset(BaseModel):
    id: int
    name: str
    description: str
    created_at: str


class FieldSpec(BaseModel):
    name: str = Field(description="Unique, non-empty field name within the version")
    type: str = Field(description="Field type, e.g. 'string' or 'integer'")
    nullable: bool


class SchemaVersionCreate(BaseModel):
    fields: list[FieldSpec] = Field(description="Non-empty list of field definitions")


class FieldInfo(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True)

    name: str
    type: str
    nullable: bool


class SchemaVersion(BaseModel):
    dataset_id: int
    dataset_name: str
    version: int
    created_at: str
    fields: list[FieldInfo]


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Read-only schema version diff
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


class FieldChangeDefinition(BaseModel):
    type: str
    nullable: bool


class VersionFieldChange(BaseModel):
    field: str
    kind: Literal["added", "removed", "changed"]
